Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the Sri Lankan chase! The umpires are out in the middle and so are the players of Bangladesh. It will be Dimuth Karunaratne to open the innings alongside Pathum Nissanka for Sri Lanka. Taskin Ahmed has the new ball in hand and is raring to go.
... The Run Chase ...

Having excelled in the field, Sri Lanka now faces a target of 165 runs in their stipulated 50 overs. Will the Sri Lankans get the score easily and start off their Asia Cup campaign with a storm? Or will Shakib Al Hasan and his men have a magic trick up their sleeves with the ball? Let's find out in the second innings as the chase is coming up next.

The man of the moment, Matheesha Pathirana is down for a quick chat. He says that he got a chance to play in ODI cricket after a bit of a break and is happy to have done well in this game. Adds that the wicket was pretty dead in the first half and hence he tried to bowl a lot of slower balls later on. Mentions that it is a bit difficult to go from T20I cricket to ODI cricket but he has managed to do well.

Matheesha Pathirana, the fast bowling sensation, showcased his prowess by capturing 4 crucial wickets for the Sri Lankan side. Sri Lanka's performance on the field was marked by its excellence, coupled with disciplined bowling that proved to be a formidable challenge for the Bangladeshi batsmen. Maheesh Theekshana, the off-spin maestro, maintained control with his spin and claimed 2 important wickets. Additionally, the all-rounders Dhananjaya De Silva and Dunith Wellalage each secured 1 wicket, contributing to the overall effectiveness of Sri Lanka's bowling effort.

Bangladesh have found themselves bowled out for a total of 164 runs in 42.4 overs after electing to bat first in the initial innings. The early loss of wickets paved the way for Najmul Hossain Shanto, who emerged as the lone batter offering substantial resistance by crafting a determined 89 runs from 122 deliveries. However, the majority of the batting lineup struggled to make a significant impact against the formidable Sri Lankan bowling unit.

The Asia Cup carnival is just getting started, and it is now time for action in Group B to kick off, where the co-host of the continental showpiece, Sri Lanka, square off against Bangladesh at the Pallekele International Cricket Stadium in Kandy. With Afghanistan being the third team in what is considered the group of death, every game in this group holds significant importance, and neither team would want to drop points this early in the tournament. When it comes to the recent performances of these two teams in the ODI format, Sri Lanka are coming off a successful ODI World Cup Qualifier campaign, whereas Bangladesh, one of the dominant sides at home, suffered a series loss against Afghanistan in their own backyard. As far as the setup of the defending champions, Sri Lanka is concerned, they have been rocked by injuries to several key players, but playing in home conditions should give them confidence. The notable absentee is the spin wizard Wanindu Hasaranga, who is still recovering from a thigh strain but, in all likelihood, should be fit for the ODI World Cup. In his absence, Maheesh Theekshana, Dunith Wellalage, and Dushan Hemantha will be expected to fill that void. Their fast bowling stocks look depleted with the likes of Dushmantha Chameera, Dilshan Madushanka, and Lahiru Kumara absent due to injuries, in which case the experienced Kasun Rajitha will have to lead the attack. Other than him, Matheesha Pathirana, Pramod Madushan, and Binura Fernando form the fast bowling group for Sri Lanka. In the ODI World Cup Qualifier held in Zimbabwe, openers Pathum Nissanka and Dimuth Karunaratne did the heavy lifting and will hold the batting together here as well. Their middle order, comprising Kusal Mendis, Sadeera Samarawickrama, and Charith Asalanka, could not get many opportunities with the bat in Zimbabwe, but they will be tested here against seemingly better bowling units. The all-rounder department is well-rounded, with skipper Dasun Shanaka providing the pace option while Dhananjaya de Silva can chip in with his off-spin to go with their batting capabilities. On the other hand, Bangladesh have come close to lifting the Asia Cup trophy in previous editions but have faltered at the final hurdle three times. After Tamim Iqbal's retirement drama, Shakib Al Hasan has been handed the captaincy, and he will be hoping to take his team all the way this time. To go with Tamim's absence due to rehab, Bangladesh suffered another big blow as their reliable opener Litton Das was ruled out of the entire tournament due to a viral fever. Anamul Haque has been named as the replacement, and he is likely to open alongside Mohammad Naim. Najmul Hossain Shanto and Mushfiqur Rahim have been Bangladesh's key batters in recent times and will play a pivotal role in the middle order. Shakib Al Hasan has not been among the runs of late, but a big tournament player like him will indeed turn up with both bat and ball. In the spin department, Mehidy Hasan has been their go-to bowler, while Nasum Ahmed has impressed as well. The experienced pace duo of Mustafizur Rahman and Taskin Ahmed will take up two out of three seam spots, while the remaining spot will be a toss-up between Hasan Mahmud and Shoriful Islam. Sri Lanka have always had the upper hand over Bangladesh in ODIs, but out of the last three meetings, Bangladesh came out on top twice. Will Bangladesh punch above their weight? Or will Sri Lanka reign supreme? We will find out together.
